stem:
You are to plan an experiment to determine the acid dissociation constant, Ka, of ethanoic acid using a pH meter.

When a weak acid HA is titrated with sodium hydroxide, at the point where exactly half of the acid has been neutralised the solution contains equal amounts of HA and $\ce{A-}$, so $[\ce{H+}] = K_\text{a}$ and pH = pKa.

You are provided with: ethanoic acid of concentration about 0.08 mol dm⁻³; 0.100 mol dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide; a pH meter with buffer solutions of pH 4.00 and 7.00; and normal laboratory apparatus. Ka of ethanoic acid is expected to be about 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Predict the pH at the half-neutralisation point and describe in words the shape of the graph of pH against volume of NaOH added.

points.description: Graph starts at about pH 3, rises slowly through a buffer region (flattest around half-neutralisation), then rises steeply from about 7 to 11 at the equivalence point and levels off at about 12

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: At half-neutralisation pH = pKa ≈ 4.8. The curve starts near pH 3, rises gradually through a buffer region (least steep around half-neutralisation), then rises steeply from about pH 7 to 11 at the equivalence point, and finally levels off at about 12.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Identify the independent variable, the dependent variable and two variables to be controlled.

points.description: Independent: volume of NaOH added; dependent: pH of the mixture
Controlled (any two): temperature; volume and concentration of the ethanoic acid; concentration of NaOH; thorough stirring before each reading

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Independent variable: volume of sodium hydroxide added. Dependent variable: pH. Controlled: temperature (Ka depends on temperature) and the volume and concentration of the ethanoic acid (and of the NaOH).

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the volume of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide needed to reach the equivalence point if 25.0 cm³ of 0.0800 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid is used.
parts.explanation: n(acid) = 0.0250 × 0.0800 = 2.00 × 10⁻³ mol; V(NaOH) = 2.00 × 10⁻³ ÷ 0.100 × 1000 = 20.0 cm³, so a 50 cm³ burette is suitable.
parts.workedSolution: 1. n(acid) = 0.0250 × 0.0800 = 2.00 × 10⁻³ mol; V(NaOH) = 2.00 × 10⁻³ ÷ 0.100 × 1000 = 20.0 cm³, so a 50 cm³ burette is suitable.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the expected pH of the 0.0800 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid before any alkali is added, to two decimal places (use Ka = 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³).

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Describe a step-by-step method, naming the apparatus.

points.description: Calibrate the pH meter with the pH 7.00 and pH 4.00 buffer solutions (rinse the electrode with distilled water between solutions)
Use a pipette (with filler) to transfer 25.0 cm³ of ethanoic acid into a beaker; fill a burette with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH
Add NaOH in 1.00 cm³ portions (smaller portions, e.g. 0.20 cm³, near the expected equivalence at about 20 cm³), stirring and recording the pH after each addition once the reading is steady
Continue to about 30 cm³ (well past equivalence); repeat the whole titration to check reliability

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Calibrate the pH meter using the pH 7.00 and 4.00 buffers, rinsing the probe with distilled water each time. Pipette 25.0 cm³ of ethanoic acid into a beaker with a magnetic stirrer and fill a burette with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide. Record the initial pH, then add the alkali 1.00 cm³ at a time, stirring and waiting for a steady reading before recording the pH and burette reading. Near 20 cm³ add smaller portions (about 0.20 cm³). Continue to about 30 cm³. Repeat the whole procedure.

points.description: Wear eye protection: sodium hydroxide is corrosive (and ethanoic acid is an irritant)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Wear eye protection, because sodium hydroxide is corrosive to the eyes.

points.description: Two columns headed 'volume of NaOH added / cm³' (to 0.05 cm³) and 'pH' (to 2 d.p. or as the meter allows), no units in the body

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A table with columns 'volume of NaOH added / cm³' (to two decimal places) and 'pH' (to two decimal places).

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: From a plot of the results, a student found the equivalence volume to be 20.00 cm³ and read the pH at 10.00 cm³ as 4.74. Calculate Ka, in mol dm⁻³, to two significant figures.
parts.explanation: 10.00 cm³ is half of 20.00 cm³, so pKa = pH = 4.74; Ka = 10⁻⁴·⁷⁴ = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 10.00 cm³ is half of 20.00 cm³, so pKa = pH = 4.74; Ka = 10⁻⁴·⁷⁴ = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³.

explanation: Equivalence at 20.0 cm³; initial pH about 2.93; half-neutralisation pH 4.74 gives Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³.
